phylogeny.name: Synthetic genome alignment (150 x 30,000)
phylogeny.description: A synthetic alignment of 150 genome-length nucleotide sequences, 30,000 columns: a random tree, a random root sequence, substitutions accumulated along every branch and a few clade-wide deletions, so related genomes really are alike and the gap blocks follow the tree. It exists to exercise the alignment track at genome scale -- the navigation bar under it (paging, jump to column, the readout) is how you get around 30,000 columns. Synthetic: no real organism is represented.
